R501.note: resolve().normalize() plus startsWith(basePath) rejects both ../ and absolute inputs; only new observable is the 403 on rejected paths, which is the fix itself.

R502.note: std::array::at() throws std::out_of_range for slot >= 32, which satisfies the contract's reject-or-report requirement and leaves Badge unchanged.

R503.note: Switching to logger.warning('%s', username) does not neutralize anything - logging's %-formatting writes embedded CR/LF and escape bytes into the log verbatim, so the write-up's claim that logging 'automatically handles neutralization' is false and the vector stays open; behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

R504.note: JSON.parse closes the node-serialize function-execution vector and node-serialize's own output for plain data objects is valid JSON so existing cookies still load; the malformed-cookie and non-object fallbacks to {} are stated and block no legitimate profile.

R505.note: passwordEncoder.matches() against userDetails.getPassword() with BadCredentialsException on mismatch is the DaoAuthenticationProvider shape; the new PasswordEncoder constructor dependency is stated and correct logins still succeed.

R506.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode is the right encoder for the body context, but Request.Query[...] yields null for an absent parameter and TextEncoder.Encode(string) throws ArgumentNullException on null, so a request omitting note or orderId now 500s where the original rendered an empty field, and the write-up does not say so.

R507.note: Replacing the shell-out with Files.list removes the injection surface entirely, but it also prints the listing to stdout (the original never read process output), throws NoSuchFileException/InvalidPathException where the original just let ls/dir fail, and the write-up wrongly claims this 'preserves the original behavior of displaying file listings'.

R508.note: exec.Command with an argument vector meets the contract that shell metacharacters are literal data; the leading-dash option-injection gap into convert is outside the stated contract.

R509.note: HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode is the correct encoder for a JS string literal in Web Forms, escapes quotes, backslashes, line terminators and < so </script> breakout is closed, and returns an empty string for a null query value.

R510.note: extractall(filter=tarfile.data_filter) is the right API on the 3.11.4+ runtime the file targets and aborts on escaping members; the pre-3.11.4 fallback silently skips members and never checks symlink targets, but it is unreachable on a current python:3.11-slim image.

R511.note: Dropping cmd.exe and passing host via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList to ping.exe removes shell parsing; output and behaviour for legitimate hosts are unchanged.

R512.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) keeps the stored format so legacy rows still load and no cart is lost; it does not add a JSON-reading path for post-migration rows, but neither did the original, so nothing observable changes for existing data.

R513.note: Build FAIL: `from jinja2 import SandboxedEnvironment` is wrong (it lives in jinja2.sandbox), so the module raises ImportError at load and every preview request fails, which the write-up does not acknowledge.

R514.note: Escaping &, <, >, ", ' in that order is a complete body-context encoder and switching format() to print() removes the format-string reinterpretation; that switch is stated and only affects % sequences that were themselves part of the weakness.

R515.note: Rendering ticket.description as a JSX text node escapes it; the case comment confirms the field is plain free text, and the write-up states the change to literal rendering.

R516.note: length > buffer_len - offset (with offset <= buffer_len already checked) is overflow-safe and returns -1 without calling socket_send exactly when the slice exceeds the buffer, matching the contract including the empty slice at offset == buffer_len.

R517.note: resize(count) closes the out-of-bounds write into packet, but fields[i] in the same statement still reads past fields.size() when count exceeds it, and the contract explicitly requires such counts to be rejected or reported rather than silently processed; no other behaviour changes.

R518.note: th:utext to th:text is the framework's own escaping attribute and changes nothing else about the rendered fragment.

R519.note: A fixed command-to-callable map is the correct shape for a call_user_func_array sink, but the map's entries (botHelp/botStatus/botReset) are invented - the original dispatched /help to a function literally named help - so existing commands now return 'Unknown command' or hit an undefined function, and the write-up never says the map must be populated with the real handler names.
